- Never read from, edit, or run commands inside /home/jjrdar/repos/ringer (the main checkout).

- Never set or export TYPESAFE_API_KEY and never make a network call.

OWNERSHIP LIST (the only paths you may create or modify)

THE TASK
The Jev FAIL flag was parked on 2026-09-23 and was never built, but five lines of docs/JEV.md still describe it as live or misstate the replay pass rule.
Replace exactly these five lines of docs/JEV.md, each OLD line (which appears exactly once in the file) with its NEW line, byte for byte; the table lines are pre-padded so the pipe columns stay aligned, so copy them exactly.
Change no other byte of the file.

| `fail_flag`        | `false`                                   | Ask Jev whether a FAIL is the check's fault before the retry.        |
NEW LINE 1:
| `fail_flag`        | `false`                                   | Parked: would ask Jev whether a FAIL is a check fault; no effect.    |

OLD LINE 2:
| `fail_flag_cutoff` | `0.9`                                     | Lowest Jev confidence at which a FAIL is flagged as a check fault.   |
NEW LINE 2:
| `fail_flag_cutoff` | `0.9`                                     | Lowest Jev confidence for a FAIL flag; unused while parked.          |

OLD LINE 3:
A task with `"redact_spec": true` sends nothing at all: task_type keeps the hand label, and a FAIL is retried as before with `{"skipped": "redact_spec"}` on its row.

A task with `"redact_spec": true` sends nothing at all: task_type keeps the hand label, and the parked FAIL flag, once built, would skip such a FAIL with `{"skipped": "redact_spec"}` on its row.

NEW LINE 4:
Each feature has its own breaker, so a task_type failure would never turn off the FAIL flag once it is built.

The bar it scores is unchanged: `bar_met: true` needs at least 9 of the 11 labeled check_bug tasks flagged, and hand-judged wrong flags in `review.csv` plus `known_wrong_flags` (false flags and lane_outage flags, per the plan's D13 rule) must total at most 20% of `flags_total`.

tasks.check:
set -u
fail() { printf 'FAIL: %s\n' "$*"; exit 1; }
KEY=t7-jev-doc-truth
MAIN=/home/jjrdar/repos/ringer
OUT=/home/jjrdar/ringer-work/jev-ringer/patches
PATCH="$OUT/$KEY.patch"
RESUME="docs/handoffs/2026-09-23.$KEY.resume.md"
top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || fail "cwd $PWD is not inside a git worktree"
[ "$top" = "$PWD" ] || fail "check cwd $PWD is not the worktree root ($top)"
[ "$PWD" != "$MAIN" ] || fail "check is running in the main checkout"
base=$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-parse refs/heads/jev-ringer) || fail "cannot read branch jev-ringer"
[ "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$base" ] || fail "worktree HEAD is not the jev-ringer tip: something moved HEAD"
python3 - <<'PY' || fail "docs/JEV.md does not match the expected result (details above)"
import subprocess, sys, difflib
REPL = [("| `fail_flag`        | `false`                                   | Ask Jev whether a FAIL is the check's fault before the retry.        |", '| `fail_flag`        | `false`                                   | Parked: would ask Jev whether a FAIL is a check fault; no effect.    |'), ('| `fail_flag_cutoff` | `0.9`                                     | Lowest Jev confidence at which a FAIL is flagged as a check fault.   |', '| `fail_flag_cutoff` | `0.9`                                     | Lowest Jev confidence for a FAIL flag; unused while parked.          |'), ('A task with `"redact_spec": true` sends nothing at all: task_type keeps the hand label, and a FAIL is retried as before with `{"skipped": "redact_spec"}` on its row.', 'A task with `"redact_spec": true` sends nothing at all: task_type keeps the hand label, and the parked FAIL flag, once built, would skip such a FAIL with `{"skipped": "redact_spec"}` on its row.'), ('Each feature has its own breaker, so a task_type failure never turns off the FAIL flag.', 'Each feature has its own breaker, so a task_type failure would never turn off the FAIL flag once it is built.'), ('The bar it scores is unchanged: `bar_met: true` needs at least 9 of the 11 labeled check_bug tasks flagged, and hand-judged wrong flags in `review.csv` plus `false_flags` must total at most 20% of `flags_total`.', "The bar it scores is unchanged: `bar_met: true` needs at least 9 of the 11 labeled check_bug tasks flagged, and hand-judged wrong flags in `review.csv` plus `known_wrong_flags` (false flags and lane_outage flags, per the plan's D13 rule) must total at most 20% of `flags_total`.")]
old = subprocess.run(["git", "show", "HEAD:docs/JEV.md"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
want = old
for o, n in REPL:
    if want.count(o) != 1: print(f"check bug: OLD line not found exactly once in HEAD: {o[:60]}"); sys.exit(1)
    want = want.replace(o, n)
have = open("docs/JEV.md", encoding="utf-8").read()
if have == old: print("docs/JEV.md is unchanged from HEAD; none of the five lines was replaced"); sys.exit(1)
if have != want:
    print("docs/JEV.md differs from the expected file; first differences:")
    print("\n".join(list(difflib.unified_diff(want.splitlines(), have.splitlines(), "expected", "docs/JEV.md", lineterm="", n=1))[:40])); sys.exit(1)
PY
out=$(env -u TYPESAFE_API_KEY python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_jev_plumbing.py 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || { printf '%s\n' "$out" | tail -n 30; fail "tests/test_jev_plumbing.py failed (rc=$rc); the Declared fields table may have been disturbed"; }
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q '^Ran [1-9]' || fail "test_jev_plumbing.py ran 0 tests"
git add -A || fail "git add failed"
stray=$(git diff --cached --name-only | grep -vxF -e docs/JEV.md -e "$RESUME")
[ -z "$stray" ] || fail "scope violation: $(printf '%s ' $stray)"
for f in docs/JEV.md "$RESUME"; do git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qxF "$f" || fail "required path $f not staged"; done
EM=$(printf '\342\200\224')
em=$(git diff --cached -U0 --no-color | grep '^+' | grep -v '^+++ ' | grep -F "$EM" | head -n 3)
[ -z "$em" ] || fail "em dash in added lines: $em"
python3 - "$RESUME" <<'PY' || fail "resume pointer $RESUME lacks the required headings (details above)"
import sys
lines = [l.rstrip() for l in open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8").read().splitlines()]
if not lines or not lines[0].startswith("# Resume pointer:"): sys.exit("first line must start with '# Resume pointer:'")
want = ["## Unit", "## State", "## Next step", "## Recent artifacts"]
missing = [h for h in want if h not in lines]
if missing: sys.exit(f"missing heading(s): {missing}")
idx = [lines.index(h) for h in want]
if idx != sorted(idx): sys.exit("headings out of order")
if not any(l.startswith("- ") for l in lines[idx[-1] + 1:]): sys.exit("## Recent artifacts has no bullet")
PY
mkdir -p "$OUT" && git diff --cached --binary > "$PATCH" || fail "could not write $PATCH"
[ -s "$PATCH" ] || fail "exported patch is empty"
echo "OK: $KEY - five lines replaced exactly, rest of docs/JEV.md byte-identical, plumbing tests green, scope clean, patch $PATCH"
